_about: Speed budgets for scripts/speed-test.mjs, in milliseconds on the REFERENCE machine (a machine where `node -e ""` takes about referenceFloorMs). The test multiplies every budget by how much slower the machine it runs on is. Budgets come from Nielsen's response-time limits (0.1 s feels instant, 1 s keeps the user's flow of thought, 10 s is the limit of attention), set well under 1 s for anything interactive. They are NOT the current speed: the current speed is about three to five times lower, and the gap is the room allowed for noise. To tighten one, change it here and say why in docs/TESTING-PLAN.md.

version.why: purix --version: process start only; the floor of every other number

help.why: purix <command> --help: start-up plus argument parsing; people type this when unsure, so it has to feel instant

read.why: read-only commands (status, check, stats, tools list ...): under the 1 s flow-of-thought limit with room to spare

write.why: light local writes (config set, lock, adopt, backup create ...)

index-small.why: purix index on a one-file project: the first command a new user runs

hook.why: purix hook ... pre-tool-use: an agent waits for this before EVERY edit, so it must stay far under 1 s

mcp-start.why: start the MCP server and finish the handshake: paid once per agent session

mcp-call.why: one MCP read tool call on a running server

scale._why: Index time must grow about in step with the project. Slope is log(time ratio) / log(size ratio) between the two largest sizes: 1.0 = in step, 2.0 = quadratic. Sizes are large on purpose: index has a fixed cost of about 150 ms, and on 25 to 300 files that cost hides growth (the old quadratic bug showed there only because it was extreme). 10 s is Nielsen's limit of attention for the largest size. abortAfterMs: if one run takes longer than this (times the machine factor) the sizes after it are not run, because a quadratic index at 8,000 files would take hours.

regression._why: With --compare: fail only if the median is more than 25% AND more than 40 ms (x machine factor) slower than a baseline saved on the same machine. Both conditions, so noise on a 90 ms command does not fail a run.
